The material shall be fine, free flowing, yellow to yellow-green homogeneous powder, free from visible extraneous matter and hard aggregates. dt shall wet readily on mixing with water, providing a suspension suitable for use as spray. 3.3 The material shall also comply requirements given in Table 1. 3.3.1 When cribed in 7.2 the observed of any of the with the

the samples shall not differ from the declared nominal value by more than the tolerance l&its indicated under 3.3.1. 4 PACKING The material up to 500 g shall be packed in trilaminate pouch ( 50 gsm paper/O'009 mm aluminium foil/O'0375 mm LDPE ), mouth heatsealed. The trilaminate pouch shall be further packed individually in cardboard cartons conforming to IS 6604 : 1972 which in term shall be packed in corrugated fibre board boxes conforming to IS 2771 ( Part 1 ) : 1977. The material above 500 g in quantity shall be packed in tinplate or mild steel containers suitably lacquered from inside or in fibre board containers. The containers shall be lined with LDPE liner of thickness not less than 0'062 mm. The containers shall also comply with the requiretients specified in 2 of IS 8190 ( Part 1 ) : 1988. 5 MARKING The containers shall bear legibly and indelibly the following information in addition to any other informafion as is necessary under the 1

ANNEX B [ Table 1, Sl No. (ii) ]
DETERMINATION
B-1 APPARATUS

OF MANCOZEB

CONTENT

The apparatus shall be assembled as shown in Fig. 1 of IS 8707 : 1978 with 4 gas absorbers. Absorbers No. 1 and No. 2 shall be lead acetate traps, where as, absorbers No. 3 and No. 4 shall be potash traps. The apparatus shall consist of 2,20-ml round bottom decomposition flask fitted with a condenser with an outlet tube connected to four absorbers and a ZOO-mlfilter flask serving as a bubbler. The latter in turn is connected to a water suction pump. B-2 REAGENTS B-2.1 Lead ( mlv ). Acetate Solution 5 N. 10 percent

B-2.2 Sulphuric Acid -

B-2.3 Glacial Acetic Acid B-2.4 Dilute Acetic Acid B-2.5 Mhanolic tion - 2 N. Potasium 30 percent ( v/v ). Hydroxide 0'1 N. Solu-

bubbles per second. Immediately add 25 ml of sulphuric acid through the inlet tube and start heating as rapidly as possible. Continue heating and reflex for 2 hours from the commencement of heating. At the end of digesion, quickly disconnect the absorbers. Transfer the contents of absorbers No. 3 and 4 ( potash traps ) into a 500-ml Erlenmeyer flask rinsing the traps thoroughly with a total of 250 ml distilled water and transferring the washings to the flask. Add few drops of phenolphthalain indicator solution and neutralise with dilute acetic acid keeping the solution cool with ice if required. Titrate the neutralised solution immediately with standard iodine solution using 5 ml starch indicator solution. B-3.2 Carry out a blank determination by taking 25 ml methanolic potassium hydroxide solution in a 500-ml Erlenmeyer flask and adding 250 ml distilled water and few drops of phenolphthalein indicator solution. Add dilute acetic acid to neutralize and then titrate with standard iodine solution using 5 ml starch indicater solution. Not more than 0'1 ml shall be consumed. B-3 ESTIMATION B-3.1 Add 25 ml each of lead acetate solution Srmilarly add 25 ml to the first two absorbers. each of methalonic potassium hydroxide solution to the last two gas absorbers. Transfer 0'35 to 0'45 g of accurately weighed sample to the 250-ml decomposition flask and connect it to the assembly. Start cooling water through the condenser. Add 50 ml of glacial acetic acid through the inlet tube which must dip in the liquid. Adjust the rate of gas bubbling to 5-10

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, types or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
